meta.title: Operation of Dissolution Test Apparatus in Pharmaceutics Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the rate and extent of drug release from solid oral dosage forms (tablets, capsules) using pharmacopeial dissolution testing methods (Apparatus I — Basket, Apparatus II — Paddle) for formulation development and quality control.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutics laboratory for dissolution testing as per IP/BP/USP specifications — a mandatory release test for oral solid dosage forms.
procedure: Fill each dissolution vessel with the specified volume of freshly prepared dissolution medium (typically 900 mL of phosphate buffer pH 6.8 or 0.1 N HCl for tablets) pre-warmed to 37 ± 0.5°C.
Verify the temperature of the medium in each vessel using a calibrated thermometer — must be 37 ± 0.5°C before starting.
Degas the dissolution medium by sonication for 10–15 minutes or by vacuum filtration to remove dissolved air (air bubbles attach to tablet surfaces and give erroneously high dissolution rates).
Select and assemble the appropriate apparatus: Apparatus I (basket) or Apparatus II (paddle) as per the product specification.
For Apparatus I: place the tablet/capsule in the stainless steel basket; lower the basket to the specified distance from the vessel bottom (25 ± 2 mm).
For Apparatus II: drop the tablet/capsule directly into the vessel (use sinkers for low-density or floating formulations).
Set the rotation speed: typically 50–100 RPM for Apparatus II (paddle); 100 RPM for Apparatus I (basket).
Withdraw samples at the specified time points (e.g., 15, 30, 45, 60 minutes) from each vessel using a pipette or automatic sampling probe — filter through 0.45 µm filter immediately.
Replace withdrawn sample volume with equal volume of fresh, pre-warmed dissolution medium.
Measure absorbance of each sample at the specified wavelength using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Calculate percentage drug dissolved at each time point using a standard calibration curve.
Accept the batch if % dissolution meets the Q-value criterion (typically Q = 75% in 45 minutes for IP/USP).
Record all temperature, rpm, time point, absorbance, and % dissolved values in the dissolution test record.
precautions: Temperature control is critical — even 1°C deviation significantly affects dissolution rate; verify all vessels before starting.
Degas the dissolution medium — undegassed medium with dissolved CO₂ causes bubble formation on the tablet surface and falsely high early dissolution readings.
Ensure the shaft is centred in the vessel — off-centre shafts cause wobble that increases dissolution rate variability.
Use sinkers for formulations that float — floating tablets give erratically high or low results depending on their position in the vessel.
Withdraw samples from the defined sampling zone (midway between the paddle and the vessel surface, 10 mm from the vessel wall) — position affects readings.
Filter samples immediately after withdrawal — unfiltered samples contain fine particles that give falsely high absorbance.
Calibrate the dissolution apparatus annually: temperature uniformity, shaft wobble, and rpm accuracy as per USP General Chapter ‹711›.
